# Frontend stack selection

Read only for greenfield UI work after loading `stack-profile`. Existing repository, design system,
browser support, and deployment constraints win.

1. Record rendering/SEO needs, navigation depth, data and live-update behavior, accessibility,
   browser support, deployment, telemetry, and team ownership.
2. Choose the smallest architecture that satisfies them. React, Vue, another maintained framework,
   or no framework can all be valid.
3. Add router, server-state cache, global state, form, table, chart, and animation libraries only for
   named capabilities. Prefer one established component/token system over incompatible resets.
4. Verify current official documentation, maintenance, bundle/runtime impact, SSR/client constraints,
   accessibility behavior, and version compatibility before selection.
5. Define production build, deep-link fallback, asset caching, CSP/security headers, health/telemetry,
   and rollback for the selected host. Deployment remains a human-owned gated effect.

TanStack, Tailwind, shadcn/Radix/Base UI, Mantine, React Testing Library, Vue Test Utils, MSW,
Playwright, and chart libraries are options—not universal dependencies or prohibitions. Match the
repository once selected and record any deliberate stack exception.
